title: Common mix-ups with def and call
idea: TOOL: spot the usual beginner mistakes - forgetting the call, wrong def line, missing colon.

exercises.prompt:
This prints nothing:

def greet():
    print("Hi")

What's missing?
exercises.explanation: The sub-plan is defined but never called. Add greet() to run it. Forgetting the call is the top mistake.

exercises.prompt:
What's wrong here?

def greet()
    print("Hi")
greet()
options: The def line is missing its colon
exercises.explanation: A def line needs a colon: 'def greet():'. Without the ':' Python can't tell the body is starting.

exercises.prompt:
What's wrong here?

def greet():
print("Hi")
greet()
options: The body print isn't indented under def
exercises.explanation: The print must be indented to be inside greet. Un-indented, it isn't part of the sub-plan.

exercises.prompt: Writing 'greet' (without the parentheses) on its own line calls the sub-plan.
exercises.explanation: No. You must write greet() with the parentheses to call it. 'greet' alone does not run the body.

exercises.prompt: A learner says 'I defined greet so Hi should have printed.' What's the misunderstanding?
options: Defining doesn't run it - you must call greet()
exercises.explanation: Classic define-vs-run mix-up. The def only describes greet; calling greet() is what makes 'Hi' print.

exercises.prompt: Which of these are REQUIRED to define and run a printing sub-plan? (Pick all.)
options: the word def and a name
a colon at the end of the def line
exercises.explanation: You need the def line (def name() :), an indented body, AND a call to run it. All four matter.

exercises.prompt:
Fix this so 'Hi' prints:

def greet():
    print("Hi")
____
exercises.explanation: Add the call greet() on the last line. Now the defined sub-plan actually runs and prints 'Hi'.

exercises.prompt: Match each mistake to its fix.
exercises.explanation: Three classic slips: missing call, missing colon, missing indent. Each has a clear, small fix.

exercises.prompt: A missing colon on the def line and a missing call cause the SAME problem.
exercises.explanation: No. A missing colon is an error in the def itself; a missing call means it's defined fine but never runs.

exercises.prompt: The safest mental check after writing a sub-plan:
options: did I both DEFINE it and CALL it?
did I use a big number?
exercises.explanation: Always check both halves: define (def...) and run (name()). Forgetting the call is the most common bug here.
